title: Kestrel and the Garden
premise: Dominic Nystrom, a bone-carver whose carved relics let him hear the voices of the dead, has spent years hiding in the Thornfell mountains after the fall of the old covenant between the human realm and the Garden—the dreaming world beneath the roots. When a mute child named Kestrel arrives at his door speaking the pre-kingdom tongue of the Garden, Dominic learns the covenant's breaking was no accident: the Warden of Winter, once his mentor, is devouring memories to freeze both realms into stillness. Guided by smugglers' roads, the voices of the carved dead, and Kestrel's growing power, Dominic must gather the scattered covenant-stones and confront the Warden at the Garden's heart. In the end, Dominic sacrifices his own memories of the dead he loves to reforge the covenant, and Kestrel—revealed as the Garden's last seed—chooses to grow among mortals, giving Dominic a new, living family to remember forward instead of back.
about_author: Lior Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funerary carvings in northern mountain villages before turning to fiction. Their work blends folkloric scholarship with a smuggler's love of back roads, bad weather, and stubborn found families.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Bones
chapters.summary: Dominic Nystrom's POV. In his mountain workshop, Dominic carves a keepsake bone and hears its dead owner's last words, establishing his gift and his self-imposed isolation after the covenant's fall. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor, and the first hint that the winter this year is falling wrong.

chapters.title: A Knock Before the Snow
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A half-frozen child appears at his door during an early blizzard, mute but unafraid, and speaks a single word in a language Dominic has only heard from thousand-year-old bones. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion cracking open a closed door.

chapters.title: What the Old Tongue Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, rendered through sensation and image. The child experiences Dominic's workshop as a place humming with voices, and the carved bones begin answering her in a language older than kingdoms. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by the terror of being hunted.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic maps the Thornfell passes and realizes the border roads have sealed themselves—something is closing the mountains. He decides Kestrel cannot stay, yet cannot be sent away. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility coming due.

chapters.title: The Warden's Frost
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. High in a fortress of still air, the Warden of Winter interrogates a captured messenger, consuming his memories, and learns a Garden-seed lives. Emotional beat: cold, patient hunger; the reader sees the clock start ticking.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ivory
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The dead speak through Dominic's oldest carving: a warning about the covenant-stones, four anchors scattered across the Thornfell that once held the two realms open. Emotional beat: grief repurposed as a map.

chapters.title: The Road That Hates Carts
chapters.summary: Dominic and Kestrel, shared POV. They take the smuggler's road toward the first stone, and Kestrel's presence makes the mountain's old magic wake—bridges of root, doors in rock. Emotional beat: first tentative trust, found-family roots taking hold.

chapters.title: The Toll at Greyford
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a river town, an old smuggling contact recognizes Kestrel's nature and must be bought or bound to silence; the town's frozen chapel shows the Warden's reach. Emotional beat: the past as both currency and debt.

chapters.title: First Stone: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Beneath Greyford's flooded quarry, Kestrel raises the first covenant-stone by singing the old tongue, and for one breath both realms overlap. Emotional beat: awe and belonging—and a distant answering cold.

chapters.title: What Dominic Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A flashback chapter: how Dominic helped break the covenant years ago, deceived by the Warden when she was still his mentor. Emotional beat: guilt revealed as the engine of his exile.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Still Air
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Warden's memory-eaten servants track the pair through a pass; a night fight on a rope bridge ends with Kestrel freezing a pursuer mid-leap, frightening even herself. Emotional beat: power's first taste of corruption.

chapters.title: The Hearth That Took Them In
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sheltering with a shepherd family who remember the old covenant in lullabies, Kestrel experiences domestic warmth for the first time. Emotional beat: found family as a promise worth fighting for.

chapters.title: Second Stone: The Choir of Roots
chapters.summary: Shared POV. In the deep forest, the second stone is guarded by the rooted dead, who demand a memory as toll. Dominic pays one—his mother's voice—and Kestrel quietly promises to remember it for him. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Ice Chapel
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The Warden offers Dominic restoration of everything he's lost if he delivers the seed. He refuses, but leaves shaken, hiding the offer from Kestrel. Emotional beat: temptation, and the first lie between them.

chapters.title: Kestrel Unbound
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel's power surges past her control; she accidentally unmakes a frozen village's grief, then nearly unmakes the villagers' love for each other. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—power that heals can also hollow.

chapters.title: The Lie Between Them
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Kestrel discovers Dominic's hidden bargain; their argument on the high moor breaks the fragile trust they've built, and she walks into the storm alone. Emotional beat: heartbreak at the story's darkest hinge.

chapters.title: Third Stone: The Teeth of the World
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Alone, Kestrel reaches the third stone in a canyon of wind and is ambushed by the Warden's servants; Dominic arrives, having chosen her over his own redemption, and they raise it together. Emotional beat: reconciliation through action, not apology.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. The Warden begins the final rite at the Garden's heart, freezing the fourth stone and with it the boundary between memory and death; across both realms, people begin forgetting their dead. Emotional beat: dread at global scale.

chapters.title: Down the Root-Roads
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Dominic and Kestrel descend through the living root-roads into the Garden itself—a place built from everything mortals have ever remembered lovingly. Emotional beat: beauty sharpened by urgency.

chapters.title: The Warden's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Confrontation in the Garden's heart: the Warden reveals she froze the realms to stop her own erasure by forgetting, and offers Dominic his dead back one final time. Emotional beat: villain and student mirrored, both grieving.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, climax. Kestrel accepts her nature as the Garden's last seed and, with Dominic paying the covenant's price—his memories of every dead voice he loves—the stones are reforged and the Warden is unmade into falling snow. Emotional beat: triumph paid for in grief.

chapters.title: What Grows After
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, resolution. Spring returns to Thornfell; Dominic remembers the dead as stories rather than voices, and Kestrel—rooted now in a cottage garden—chooses to grow among mortals. The found family plants something new. Emotional beat: quiet hope, memory turned toward the living.
